question: What is the difference between being near a river and being inside an official flood zone?
answer:
Being near a river means residing in proximity to a water body, while being in an official flood zone signifies that the area is designated as susceptible to flooding based on specific criteria and maps.
• The "Floodway" and "Zone AE" are identified on Flood Insurance Rate Maps and include lands adjacent to water bodies that are reserved to allow base flood flow without significantly increasing water elevation.
• Zone AE encompasses lands susceptible to base flooding between the limits of the major channel and the flood plain, excluding the major channel lands themselves.
• Zone A refers to lands within the limits of the major channel, which is the bed of a river, stream, creek, or natural drainage, and adjacent portions reserved for base flood discharge.
• Zone A includes areas subject to base flooding associated with rivers, lakes, and lagoons.
• Zone AE includes areas subject to base flooding with waves less than 1.5 feet high.

question: What should I review before proposing a garden, park, or community center on a vacant lot?
answer:
Before proposing a garden, park, or community center on a vacant lot, you should review requirements for common open space, integration with existing developments, and environmental considerations.
• Developments will have usable public spaces such as lawns, gardens, patios, plazas, gazebos, and recreational areas, ensuring all micro-homes have access to them.
• The main common area should be centrally located within the project.
• Community buildings or recreational facilities can be counted towards the calculation of common open spaces.
• Additional common space can only represent twenty-five percent (25%) of the total requirement, with pathways connecting the entire development.
• Passive pathways are permitted and can count towards the common open space requirement.
• Thirty-five (35) square meters of common open space per unit are required.
• Fifty percent (50%) of the units must have their main entrance facing the common open space.
• The design and construction of parks or outdoor recreational facilities should minimally impact the area, protect the land, avoid impermeabilization, and preserve vegetation and topographic features.
• Areas promoting the preservation of large open spaces for public recreation will not permit land segregation, except when dedicating a portion for public use to a competent entity via public deed.
• In this district, land subdivision will not be permitted, except when dedicating a portion of the D-A district for public use.
• The plan proposes fostering the reuse of vacant lots and rehabilitated structures within the urban core.
• It is also proposed to promote the integration of new developments into existing urban development and future developments, emphasizing continuity.
• The plan encourages maximizing developed areas and existing infrastructure and public services through construction on vacant lots and reconstruction, before developing land outside urban areas.
• The purpose of the CUT-P District is to classify land for plazas and parks for active and passive recreation, ensuring their location is in harmony with land use public policies and compatible with their immediate surroundings.

• A municipal recovery plan aims for municipal recovery by considering territorial uses, conditions, and public policy instruments.
• A Mitigation Plan is a plan against hazards.
